before: 2024 #StrikeGermany withdrawals kept as a Red flag point; 2025 letter quoted 'In 2026, no exhibition is planned alongside the festival' as the letter's words and said it was 'forwarded' with unspecified signatories
after: 2024 withdrawals moved to Wider context with the connection stated; the 2025 open letter stays as the only Red flag point, dated 1 February 2025 (Bartholl, SPECTRE) and forwarded to nettime 2 February 2025 by Broeckmann; the 'media-theoretical conference' line is Ursula Damm's, not the letter's
reason: Spike (Adina Glickstein, 'The Highs and Lows of transmediale 2024', 14 February 2024) says #StrikeGermany asked artists to withdraw from publicly funded German institutions 'such as transmediale' and opposed the Berlin Senate clause and German state policy; transmediale's own 19 January statement condemned the clause. The target was the Senate and German state policy, not transmediale or the Kulturstiftung des Bundes, so it is Wider context. The nettime letter (signed by !Mediengruppe Bitnik, Aram Bartholl, Constant Dullaart, Danja Vasiliev) is addressed to transmediale e.V. (Filippo Gianetta, Magdalena Ritter) and its advisory board, so the flag stays. Funding by Kulturstiftung des Bundes since 2004 verified on transmediale.de/en/about, the KSB project page and Kulturprojekte Berlin.
